{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Given severe right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA. If variance heterogeneity is severe, Welch's ANOVA as alternative.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73; standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or generalized linear mixed model with binomial family. If ANOVA insisted upon, arcsine transformation is outdated; logistic regression preferred.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Extreme right skew (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) and presence of values >>1 suggest outliers or calculation artifacts. Log-transformation recommended; if transformation fails, non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Moderate right skew (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50); assess normality and homoscedasticity. Robust ANOVA or Welch's ANOVA if variance inequality across paradigms.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38, sd 0.24; distribution likely beta-like. Standard ANOVA may be acceptable if residuals satisfactory, but beta regression or arcsine-square-root transformation worth considering. Check for floor/ceiling effects near boundaries."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures—8 mice with 7,233-10,986 trials each. Standard ANOVA assumes independence; mouse-level clustering requires mixed-effects models or mouse as random effect.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each response. Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency severely non-normal; AD moderately non-normal; Average Speed moderately skewed; Success is binary.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's or Bartlett's test across 5 paradigms. Given unequal sample sizes (Combined n=48,846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3,323), variance heterogeneity likely.",
    "Outliers: Examine extreme values in Time-to-Target (max 201.4s), Path Efficiency (max 29.8), Average Speed (max 75.4 cm/s) for data entry errors or genuine extreme performance.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined paradigm dominates (63.7% of data); power for Bright Visual Only and Sham comparisons limited."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant (or meaningful effect size): pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for ANOVA-compatible variables, controlling family-wise error rate.",
    "For unequal variances: Games-Howell post-hoc test.",
    "For non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis: Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction.",
    "For logistic regression: pairwise odds ratios with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment.",
    "Focus contrasts: Combined vs each single-modality (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and vs Sham; sensory-only vs Sham; ICMS vs sensory-only to assess additive/synergistic effects.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables, Cramer's V or odds ratios for Success, eta-squared/omega-squared for ANOVA."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm likely shows fastest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, and highest Path Efficiency given largest sample size and presumed optimal stimulation design.",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance (slowest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, highest AD indicating more erratic paths).",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only conditions on speed metrics but underperform on path efficiency if proprioceptive guidance alone produces faster but less directed movement.",
    "Dim vs Bright Visual Only: uncertain direction; dim may reduce distraction or impair detection, while bright may enhance salience or cause glare/avoidance. Sample sizes differ substantially (Dim n=9,603 vs Bright n=3,323).",
    "AD expected lowest in Combined and ICMS Only (straighter paths), highest in Sham and possibly Bright Visual Only if visual distraction increases meandering.",
    "Success rate differences may be modest given ceiling effects (overall mean 0.73)."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance across paradigms (Combined 48,846 vs Bright Visual Only 3,323) reduces power for specific comparisons and inflates Type I error risk for underrepresented groups.",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored in standard ANOVA—mouse-level clustering induces pseudoreplication and underestimated standard errors. Mixed-effects models required for valid inference.",
    "Binary Success variable violates ANOVA assumptions; logistic or mixed-logistic regression necessary.",
    "Path Efficiency values >>1 suggest calculation anomalies or extreme path looping requiring investigation before analysis.",
    "No covariates for learning effects, trial order, or session effects; performance may change within and across sessions.",
    "Temperature fixed at 0.25 for LLM generation; no uncertainty quantification from model sampling.",
    "Single data view (summary_only) prevents access to raw trial-level data for diagnostic visualization."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept; use generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family for Success. Include trial number or session as additional random or fixed effect to account for learning. Compare models with likelihood ratio tests, report marginal means with 95% confidence intervals, and conduct planned contrasts (Combined vs others, Sham vs active conditions) with multiplicity adjustment. If computational constraints prevent mixed models, aggregate to mouse-level means and apply standard ANOVA with reduced power but valid independence assumption."
}
